events.text:
You are doing a careful, mechanical Lean 4 port inside the Archon Horizon workspace. Read the lean-check skill at /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/lean-check/SKILL.md first and FOLLOW ITS LSP LOOP (lean_diagnostic_messages / lean_goal before and after each edit; do not drive this with lake build).

PROJECT: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild (work from this directory).

THE TASK. Port a stalk-evaluation engine from the chart-typed carrier `DivisorAdaptation` to the widened carrier `AffAdaptation`, into the EXISTING file:
  AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStalkEval.lean
That file already exists, is rooted in AlgebraicJacobian.lean, and currently has exactly TWO `sorry`s, at:
  - `AffAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor`
  - `AffAdaptation.IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor`
Its first two lemmas (`span_eq_of_unit_mul`, `span_germ_eqn_eq_stalkIdeal`, `isUnit_germ_eqn_of_coeffAt_eq_zero`) are already proved — do not change them.

SOURCES TO PORT FROM (read them fully):
  - AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyStalkEval.lean (349 lines) — declarations from line 124 onward: `mem_span_singleton_of_isUnit_or_mem`, `stalkColEval`, `stalkColEval_mk`, `ovlStalkColEval`, `ovlStalkColEval_toOvlLeft`, `ovlStalkColEval_toOvlRight`, `stalkColEval_glued`, `eqn_ne_zero`, `moduleFinite_stalkQuot`, `finrank_stalkQuot_eq_coeffAt_mul`.
  - AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean (409 lines) — the engine: `pieceStalkEval` and its injectivity/surjectivity/bijectivity, `gluedStalkEval`, `gluedStalkEval_injective`, `pieceTarget`, `gluedStalkEval_surjective`, and finally `deg_presentationDivisor` (line 324) and `IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor` (line 365).

THE SUBSTITUTION RULE, and it is the whole point of the port. The chart-typed side indexes pieces through a `Sum` index inside `FinCoverData` and types each piece into one of two pinned P1 charts. The widened side (`AffCoverData`, structure at AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean:145) has `pieces : Fin m -> Opens`, `isAffineOpen` and `cover` as FIELDS. So:
  - `A.pieces j` becomes `D.pieces j`; `A.index` becomes `D.index`; likewise `A.isAffineOpen_pieces` becomes `D.isAffineOpen_pieces`.
  - The chart-typed `exists_mem_pieces` (DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:179-185) proves its goal from `relCover_sup` + `cover0` + `cover1`. DO NOT PORT THAT PROOF. On the widened side use the already-existing `D.exists_mem_pieces` (AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean:166), which is the structure field.
  - Everything else should transcribe with names unchanged. `AffAdaptation` carries `eqn`, `eqn_rel`, `eqn_regular`, `colength`, `ovlColength`, `ovlIdeal`, `toOvlLeft`, `toOvlRight`, `chartProd`, `ovlProd`, `deltaLeft`, `deltaRight`, `gluedSubmodule`, `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`, `Glued`, and `IsCertified` with the same clause names.

EXPECTED OUTCOME: the two `sorry`s in DivisorFamilyAffStalkEval.lean are replaced by real proofs, and any helper declarations they need are added to that same file above them (in `namespace AffAdaptation`). The file must end with ZERO sorries and ZERO errors.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS:
1. Edit ONLY AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStalkEval.lean. Do not touch any other file — other agents are working in this repo concurrently and a stray edit destroys their work. Do NOT run git commands at all.
2. If a source declaration is `private`, you cannot reference it; copy it into our file as `private` with a docstring saying where it came from and that it is private there.
3. Do not weaken any statement to make it go through. If a step genuinely needs a hypothesis the widened carrier lacks, STOP and report exactly which declaration and which step, leaving that one as `sorry` with a comment. An honest partial port is the required outcome in that case — do not invent a side condition, and do not add a hypothesis to `deg_presentationDivisor` (its whole value is that it has NO separation hypothesis).
4. Preserve `omit [...] in` lines where the source has them; the linter will tell you which instances are unused (it reports "automatically included section variable(s) unused").
5. Write docstrings in the house style of the surrounding file: state what the lemma says mathematically, and where a step differs from the chart-typed original, say so.
6. Keep `set_option` lines at the top of the file as they are.

VERIFY AS YOU GO with lean_diagnostic_messages. When you believe it is complete, run `lake build AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffStalkEval` ONCE in the foreground and report its exit code and the sorry count.

REPORT BACK: the final sorry count, the build exit code, a list of the declarations you added, and — most importantly — any place where the port was NOT verbatim, with the reason. If you left a sorry, say precisely what blocked it.

2	name: lean-check
3	description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
4	---
5	
6	## Required proof loop
7	
8	Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
9	at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
10	`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
11	before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
12	search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.
13	
14	Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
15	check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
16	validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
17	unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
18	usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
19	the check.
20	
21	LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
22	module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
23	configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
24	the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
25	only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
26	specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.
27	
28	- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
29	  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
30	  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
31	- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
32	  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
33	  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
34	  project root.
35	- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
36	  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
37	- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
38	- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
39	  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
40	- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
41	  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.
42	
43	## Fast LSP proving loop
44	
45	The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
46	(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:
47	
48	- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
49	  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
50	- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
51	  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
52	- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
53	  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
54	  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
55	- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
56	  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
57	  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
58	  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.
59	
60	Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
61	skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
62	candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
63	kernel-check the module at the end.
64	
65	## Heavy builds — actually wait for them
66	
67	Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
68	deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
69	ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
70	or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
71	"Warnings are work").
72	
73	A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
74	most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
75	build to finish**:
76	
77	- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
78	  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
79	  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
80	  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
81	- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
82	  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
83	  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
84	  is *not* done.
85	- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
86	  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
87	  for final validation.
88	- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
89	  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
90	  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
91	  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
92	- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
93	  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
94	  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
95	  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.
96	
97	## When the LSP dies on big import files
98	
99	The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
100	imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
101	that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
102	run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
103	proof error:
104	
105	- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
106	  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
107	  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
108	- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
109	  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
110	  the specific module you are proving in instead.
111	- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
112	  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyFieldCRT
9	
10	/-!
11	# The colength↔degree identity on the WIDENED adaptation, with NO separation hypothesis
12	
13	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffFieldDegree.lean` ports the *support-separated* colength↔degree identity
14	to `AffAdaptation`.  That route works, but its `hsep` is a real restriction and it has no
15	producer: a `work-reviewer` audit this session closed a refutation showing that `hsep` together
16	with a support point in `V₀ ⊓ V₁` gives `False`, and a conclusion-position census over the whole
17	project found zero producers of either separation shape.  So the separated identity's
18	"the DD-1c backward map satisfies it by construction" was inherited prose with nothing behind it.
19	
20	The chart-typed side already retired that route.  `DivisorAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor`
21	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:324`) proves the identity for **every** adaptation, with no
22	separation hypothesis at all, by evaluating the glued equalizer at stalks over the support
23	(`gluedStalkEval` bijective) instead of decomposing it over the cover.  This file ports that
24	route, which is the one a consumer should use.
25	
26	## Why this port is cheaper than it looks
27	
28	The stalk route touches the cover *less* than the separated route did, not more.  Measured:
29	`Picard/DivisorFamilyStalkEval.lean` contains **zero** chart-specific tokens, and
30	`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean` contains exactly four, all inside one block
31	(`:181-184`) whose entire output is "every point lies in some piece" — the same
32	`AffCoverData.exists_mem_pieces` substitution that carried the separated port.  Every member the
33	engine reads (`pieces`, `index`, `eqn`, `eqn_regular`, `colength`, `ovlColength`, `ovlIdeal`,
34	`chartProd`, `Glued`, `gluedSubmodule`, `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`) is carried by `AffAdaptation`
35	under the same name.
36	
37	## Main declarations
38	
39	* `AffAdaptation.span_germ_eqn_eq_stalkIdeal` — a piece equation generates `d`'s stalk ideal at
40	  each of its points, so the piece-local data is adaptation-free at stalks.
41	* `AffAdaptation.isUnit_germ_eqn_of_coeffAt_eq_zero` — vanishing coefficient means unit germ.
42	* `AffAdaptation.stalkColEval`, `stalkColEval_mk` — the piece colength evaluated at a stalk.
43	* `AffAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor` — **the identity with no `hsep`**, for every widened
44	  adaptation.
45	* `AffAdaptation.IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor` — `deg D = n`, unconditionally on the cover.
46	
47	## What this does NOT close
48	
49	`hdegAff` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffAbel.lean`) is the *Abel-value* ledger and remains an explicit
50	hypothesis there; the distance to it is the widened transport from the presentation divisor's
51	degree to the Picard class.  Nothing here touches `rep` or any antecedent of the atlas assembly.
52	-/

69	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

73	variable [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
74	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
75	  [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

77	variable {D : AffCoverData C K} {d : (relCurve C K).LocalEquations} (A : AffAdaptation D d)

79	/-- Two elements differing by a unit factor span the same ideal.  A pure five-line commutative
80	ring fact, copied because both existing statements of it are `private` — in
81	`Picard/DivisorStalkIdeal.lean:155` (as `Scheme.LocalEquations.span_eq_of_unit_mul`) and in
82	`Picard/DivisorFamilyStalkEval.lean:69` (as `DivisorAdaptation.span_eq_of_unit_mul`, itself
83	labelled a file-local copy of the first).  `private` makes them invisible to name search as well
84	as to use, so this is the third copy rather than the second; the right fix is to make one of them
85	public, which is a change to another lane's file and not mine to make mid-session. -/
86	private lemma span_eq_of_unit_mul {S : Type u} [CommRing S] {a b c : S} (hc : IsUnit c)
87	    (h : a = c * b) : Ideal.span {a} = Ideal.span {b} := by
88	  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := hc
89	  refine le_antisymm (Ideal.span_singleton_le_span_singleton.mpr ⟨u, by rw [h, mul_comm]⟩)
90	    (Ideal.span_singleton_le_span_singleton.mpr ⟨(↑u⁻¹ : S), ?_⟩)
91	  rw [h, mul_comm (u : S) b, mul_assoc, Units.mul_inv, mul_one]
92	
93	omit [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
94	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
95	  [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] in
96	/-- **A piece equation generates the stalk ideal of `d` at each of its points**, widened. -/
97	lemma span_germ_eqn_eq_stalkIdeal (j : D.index) {z : relCurve C K} (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) :
98	    Ideal.span {((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)}
99	      = d.stalkIdeal z := by
100	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
101	  have hzW : z ∈ D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
102	  have hgerm := congrArg ((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ
103	    (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
104	  rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at hgerm
105	  exact span_eq_of_unit_mul (u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ
106	    (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom) hgerm
107	
108	/-- Where the divisor coefficient vanishes, the piece equation is a stalk unit, widened. -/
109	lemma isUnit_germ_eqn_of_coeffAt_eq_zero (j : D.index) {z : relCurve C K}
110	    (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) (hzg : z ≠ genericPoint (relCurve C K))
111	    (h0 : coeffAt hzg (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation) = 0) :
112	    IsUnit (((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)) := by
113	  have hη : genericPoint (relCurve C K) ∈ D.pieces j :=
114	    Scheme.genericPoint_mem_of_nonempty ⟨z, hz⟩
115	  have hne : ((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) (genericPoint (relCurve C K))
116	      hη).hom (A.eqn j) ≠ 0 :=
117	    mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero.mp (A.eqn_regular j (genericPoint (relCurve C K)) hη)
118	  set g : (relCurve C K).functionFieldˣ := Units.mk0 _ hne with hgdef
119	  have hg : (g : (relCurve C K).functionField)
120	      = ((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) (genericPoint (relCurve C K)) hη).hom
121	          (A.eqn j) := rfl
122	  have h1 := A.coeffAt_eq_toAdd_ordZ_eqn j hz hzg g hg
123	  rw [h0] at h1
124	  have hord : Scheme.ordZ (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hzg g = 1 :=
125	    Multiplicative.toAdd.injective (by rw [h1]; exact toAdd_one.symm)
126	  exact (Scheme.isUnit_germ_iff_ordZ_eq_one K hη (A.eqn j) g hg hz hzg).mpr hord
127	
128	/-- **The colength↔degree identity for EVERY widened adaptation** — no separation hypothesis. -/
129	theorem deg_presentationDivisor :
130	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation)
131	      = (finrank K A.Glued : ℤ) := by
132	  sorry
133	
134	/-- **`deg D = n` for every widened certified adaptation**, with no hypothesis on the cover. -/
135	theorem IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor {n : ℕ} (hc : A.IsCertified n) :
136	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation) = (n : ℤ) := by
137	  sorry
